goal: Implement a reusable, fail-closed Minis GPT -> official Gemini Pro web agent -> GitHub -> GPT orchestration CLI, then test it. This is production work, not a connectivity marker.
constraints: Only this repository and branch. Keep main and README unchanged. No PR/merge, credentials, env dumps, APIs requiring new billing, account tokens, private backend endpoints, background services, schedules, Skills or global Minis changes.

Use Python 3 standard library only. Local runtime is iOS Minis Alpine aarch64. Existing authenticated executables: minis-browser-use and minis-mcp-cli; never shell=True. MCP server name GitHub. Official web project is 561adc82-06e6-4c8c-862f-3ac493b947c1 at https://antigravity.google.com/remote. Runtime scripts will be downloaded and run by GPT; do not assume these executables exist in your cloud sandbox. Mock them in cloud unit tests.

Only invoke official Antigravity webpage UI via DOM/browser actions. Do NOT extract/reuse cookies or OAuth tokens, impersonate a first-party HTTP client, use hidden React internals, bypass disabled buttons or verification, or invoke undocumented backend endpoints.
Use included Pro subscription only; stop and report if unavailable; no paid credits or billing changes. No infinite retry. Record authentication/verification failures as blocked.

No autonomous polling loops or sleeps. Each CLI command performs a bounded action and exits. GPT uses Minis shell delay between status calls. App suspension is not guaranteed to continue orchestration.
requirements: CLI commands: validate (pure local contract validation), submit, status, collect. All arguments discoverable through --help. Support --state-dir for a local job journal and --tab-id override; discover a matching official tab or open it normally. Never store a permanent tab id.

Contract fields: task_id, attempt (positive integer, not bool), goal, base_branch, allowed_write_paths (explicit relative files), acceptance (nonempty list). Fixed repo yinanan77/gemini-bridge. Derived job branch gpt-gemini/jobs/<task_id>; snapshots jobs/<task_id>/attempt-<NN>/task.json and result.json. Restrict task IDs to safe ASCII identifiers. Reject absolute/traversal/.git/.github/workflow/secrets paths, main job branch, empty/duplicate paths, malformed contract and unsupported repository. Compute canonical contract_sha256. Allowed paths include only contract and result snapshots plus explicitly authorized artifact files.

submit: create isolated job branch from specified base_branch only on attempt1; persist immutable task snapshot via authenticated GitHub MCP. For later attempts, preserve previous snapshots and require existing job journal/branch. Retrieve GitHub snapshots to reconcile failures; don't overwrite an existing different contract. Focus+execCommand(selectAll) in one browser call, then next call dispatch ClipboardEvent(DataTransfer text/plain) paste, then separately read text and send button state. Navigate official project URL for a new conversation. Validate exact full draft text, expected project/model, and non-disabled send button before clicking. Never modify disabled. UI parser can receive data.text as a JSON string or human-readable text; tolerate envelope. No automatic double submit on timeout: journal an uncertain state BEFORE sending, reconcile by task marker visible in official conversation; second submit must not send same task again.

The sent task prompt must tell Gemini to fetch/read the exact task snapshot from its GitHub job branch, implement goal inside allowed files, actually execute tests, preserve inputs and prior results, commit/push outputs on the same job branch, and write JSON result with task_id, attempt, contract_sha256, status, summary, artifacts, tests. No self-referential final commit SHA in result manifest; collector obtains authoritative branch head from GitHub.

status: inspect official UI and conversation URL; classify running, blocked (identity/quota/permission/error), or returned without claiming acceptance. Save bounded sanitized evidence. Do not classify prompt text or repeated result text as proof of success; a running=false plus error is blocked. Preserve attempts and terminal errors, not just last success.

collect: use GitHub MCP to fetch attempt result.json plus each artifact at authoritative branch head. Validate task_id/attempt/contract hash/status, allowlisted artifact paths, real file contents; reject missing/mismatched/out-of-scope data. Never run returned shell commands or downloaded code automatically. Return collected_not_accepted plus local artifact paths/commit/evidence for GPT independent review. GPT alone accepts or asks revision via attempt+1. Preserve result hashes and failures. Avoid outputting unrelated repo/account information or secrets.

Provide a dry-run/preview mode that cannot send messages or mutate GitHub. Unit tests mock all CLI I/O and cover path validation, invalid repo/ID/bool attempts, stable contract hashing, MCP text/resource envelopes, malformed outputs, paste ordering and disabled-send handling, timeout/uncertain journal, idempotent duplicate submit, result identity/hash/artifact allowlist validation, prompt-injection strings handled as data, and preservation across revisions.

WORKFLOW.md in concise Chinese must show exact GPT operating steps (contract -> submit -> bounded status -> collect -> independent tests -> accept/revise), real CLI examples, limits, and how to resume after app interruption without duplicate submissions. Do not claim native model provider integration, automatic GitHub Issue triggers, background guarantee, or zero cost. Explain this calls the official web agent with existing Pro login and requires initial/occasional human verification.

Run python3 -m unittest discover -s bridge -p test_bridge.py and python3 -m py_compile bridge/minis_gemini_bridge.py, fix actual issues, then commit and push only authorized deliverables. result.json includes actual test command, passed/failed, runtime unverified limitations, and final file list. Return branch, commit, test totals and short blockers. Keep implementation small and maintainable; do not add a framework.
acceptance: GPT will retrieve actual files through GitHub MCP, review critical subprocess/security/idempotency paths, run independent local tests, then use this CLI to submit a real second development task to Gemini and collect/test its pushed artifacts. Saving files or passing only your own mocks does not constitute end-to-end acceptance.
